title: Sequential Spinodal Decompositions and Ordering Reactions in an As-Quenched Cr<sub>39</sub>Co<sub>18</sub>Fe<sub>18</sub>Ni<sub>18</sub>Al<sub>7</sub> High-Entropy Alloy.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Arc-melted and homogenized single-phase bcc (A2) Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 (at.%) solid solution, solutionized near 1150–1250 C and water-quenched.
recollection.intervention: Guess: Rapid quench from the single-phase field followed by ex-situ characterization (APT, HRTEM, synchrotron/XRD, possibly DSC) of the as-quenched state to resolve nanoscale decomposition and ordering.
recollection.structure: Guess: A hierarchical nanostructure formed on quench consisting of a Cr-rich A2 matrix containing interconnected, nanoscale Fe/Co/Ni/Al-rich regions that are B2 ordered. The microstructure shows composition-wave modulations (spinodal) with a primary wavelength ~2–4 nm and B2 anti-phase domains a few nanometers across; overall B2 volume fraction ~0.25–0.35. No sigma phase in the as-quenched condition.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Sequential reactions during quench: (1) The supersaturated bcc (A2) crosses a miscibility gap and undergoes spinodal decomposition into Cr-rich A2 and Fe/Co/Ni/Al-rich A2; (2) Rapid short-range diffusion and strong Ni–Al ordering drive B2 formation within the Fe/Co/Ni/Al-rich regions; (3) Possible secondary, finer spinodal sharpening within the Cr-rich A2. Partitioning is governed by positive mixing enthalpies involving Cr with Ni/Al and strong Ni–Al ordering tendency.
recollection.results: Guess: APT shows strong partitioning: B2 domains enriched in (Ni+Co+Fe) ~60–70 at% and (Al+Cr) ~30–40 at%, with Al ~20–25 at% and Cr ~10–20 at% on the B2 sublattice; complementary A2 matrix ~45–55 at% Cr, Al <2 at%, Ni ~8–12 at%. Primary modulation wavelength ~2–4 nm in the as-quenched state; weak {100} B2 superlattice reflections in XRD/TEM. Estimated B2 volume fraction ~28–35% based on Al balance. As-quenched hardness plausibly elevated (≈450–600 HV) due to the nanomodulated A2/B2 structure (mechanical data may not have been reported).

score.note: The intervention is incorrect because it omits the 1100–1300 °C annealing series and instead describes only quenching and characterization. The structure broadly captures a Cr-rich BCC/A2 matrix with Ni–Al-rich B2 nanoscale regions, but misses the reciprocal BCC-within-B2 hierarchy and minor FCC, and gives inaccurate size and volume-fraction estimates. The sequential spinodal-decomposition followed by Ni–Al-driven B2 ordering mechanism is specific and substantially correct. Several guessed compositions are close to the reported matrix and particle compositions, although the proposed 2–4 nm modulation and 28–35% B2 fraction disagree with the reported 2–100 nm hierarchy and approximately 50 vol.% fine B2 at 1300 °C.
